name: Gradient Boosting Machines (GBM)
description: Gradient Boosting is an ensemble technique that builds trees sequentially, where each new tree corrects errors made by previous trees. It minimizes a loss function by adding trees that follow the negative gradient (steepest descent) of the loss, creating a strong learner from weak learners.

concept.additiveModel: F_M(x) = Σ(γₘ × hₘ(x)) where hₘ are weak learners
concept.gradientDescentInFunctionSpace: Each tree fits the negative gradient of loss function
concept.forwardStagewise: Trees added one at a time, previous trees frozen
concept.explanation: Start with initial prediction. Calculate residuals (errors). Train new tree to predict residuals. Update prediction: new_prediction = old_prediction + learning_rate × tree_prediction. Repeat.
concept.shrinkage: Learning rate controls contribution of each tree (prevents overfitting)

nEstimators.impact: More trees = better fit but risk of overfitting

learningRate.impact: Lower = need more trees but better generalization

maxDepth.impact: Controls complexity; higher = more prone to overfitting

subsample.description: Fraction of samples for fitting each tree

preprocessing: No scaling strictly required but can help
training: Initialize with constant prediction (mean for regression, log-odds for classification)
For m = 1 to M (number of trees):
- Update model: F_m = F_{m-1} + learning_rate × tree_m
tuning: Grid search or randomized search over key parameters

pros: Often best-in-class accuracy on tabular data
cons: Longer prediction time than linear models

comparisons.vsRandomForest: GBM builds sequentially (bias reduction); RF builds independently (variance reduction)
comparisons.vsXGBoost: XGB adds regularization, parallelization, handles missing values better
comparisons.vsLightGBM: LightGBM faster with large datasets, leaf-wise vs level-wise growth
